original_question: Let C(a_n) be a central Cantor set determined by its ratios of dissection (a_n). If the difference set C(a_n) - C(a_n) has nonempty interior, must 0 belong to the interior of C(a_n)?
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant family of sets (central Cantor sets encoded by dissection ratios) and the intended implication: whether nonempty interior of the self-difference set forces interior at the distinguished point 0. This is the substance of the paper’s Problem 14, up to notation and one crucial target-set typo in the conclusion. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285))
missing_details: The conclusion should concern the difference set C(a)-C(a), not the Cantor set C(a) itself. In the paper, the question is whether 0 belongs to int(C(a)-C(a)); as written, asking whether 0 is interior to C(a) is not the intended problem.
The paper quantifies over all central Cantor sets C(a), not a single fixed example.

The notation C(a) should be defined stand-alone: a=(a_n)_{n\ge 1} is the sequence of dissection ratios, and C(a) is the central Cantor set obtained from [0,1] by removing centered open intervals stage by stage according to those ratios.
The difference set should be defined explicitly as C(a)-C(a):=\{x-y:x,y\in C(a)\}.
The ambient space for interior is \mathbb{R}; thus int(C(a)-C(a)) means ordinary interior in \mathbb{R}.
To match the paper’s setup, one should state that the fundamental interval is [0,1], since that is the default convention in the surrounding discussion.
The paper writes C(a) for the whole ratio sequence a, rather than C(a_n) as a bare symbol.
refined_question: Let a=(a_n)_{n\ge 1} be a sequence of dissection ratios for a central Cantor set, and let C(a)\subset[0,1] be the corresponding central Cantor set obtained by starting from [0,1] and, at stage n, removing from each basic interval its centered open subinterval so that the two remaining closed subintervals each have length a_n times the length of their parent interval. If the algebraic difference set C(a)-C(a):=\{x-y:x,y\in C(a)\} has nonempty interior in \mathbb{R}, must 0 belong to \operatorname{int}(C(a)-C(a))?
justification: The nearest official formulation is not a conjecture from the introduction but Section 3, Problem 14. The surrounding context first introduces central Cantor sets, fixes the default fundamental interval [0,1], explains the notation C(a) arising from the sequence of dissection ratios, and notes the symmetry of central Cantor sets about 1/2, which is why self-difference sets are the natural object here. Immediately after Problem 14, the paper explains that a positive answer would simplify criteria for proving that the difference of a central Cantor set is a Cantor set, because one would only need to control gaps tending to 0. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285))
